 St Clement of Alexandria:

The Phallic Cult of Dionysus 

The Sory of Dionysus and Prosymnus [See Wikipedia: 
Prosymnus
]

[The] contests andÂ 
phalloi
Â consecratedÂ to Dionysus were a world's shame, pervading life with their deadly influence. For Dionysus, eagerly desiring to descend to Hades, did notÂ knowÂ the way; aÂ man, by name Prosymnus, offers to tell him, not without reward. The reward was a disgraceful one, though not so in the opinion of Dionysus: it was an Aphrodisian favour that was asked of Dionysus as a reward. The god was not reluctant to grant the request made to him, and promises to fulfil it should he return, and confirms his promise with anÂ oath. Having learned the way, he departed and again returned: he did not find Prosymnus, for he had died. In order to acquit himself of his promise to his lover, he rushes to his tomb, and burns with unnaturalÂ lust. Cutting a fig-branch that came to his hand, he shaped the phallus, and so performed his promise to the dead man. As a mystic memorial of this incident,Â 
phalloi
Â are raised aloft inÂ honourÂ of Dionysus through the various cities.Â For did they not make a procession inÂ honourÂ of Dionysus, and sing most shameless songs inÂ honourÂ of the pudenda, all would go wrong,Â says Heraclitus. Â This is that Pluto and Dionysus in whoseÂ honourÂ they give themselves up to frenzy, and play the bacchanal â not so much, in my opinion, for the sake of intoxication, as for the sake of the shameless ceremonial practiced. With reason, therefore, such as have become slaves of theirÂ passionsÂ are your gods!
